title: Rivermark - Renewal & Geo Provisioning Review
summary: Quarterly renewal discussion focused on adding EU and APAC regions and a capacity uplift. Customer leaning toward dedicated capacity for predictability; exploring private VPC for EU data. Agreed to run a short perf benchmark and contract amendment draft.
action_items: Aisha Khan - Provide current qps and 95th p95 latency histogram by 2025-02-19
Priya Nair (Redwood SE) - Run targeted benchmark using Rivermark prompt set; deliver results by 2025-02-21
Liam O'Connor - Draft 9‑month contract amendment with EU/APAC addendum and proposed capacity uplift; share by 2025-02-20
Marisol Vega - Send procurement templates and preferred PO wording by 2025-02-18
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and ISO27001 attestation links and private deployment checklist
SE to schedule benchmark run and invite Aisha's infra engineer
AE to share pricing workbook and draft amendment
Follow-up call scheduled for 2025-02-24 16:00 UTC to review benchmark and contract
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date/Time: 2025-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (Rivermark, Head of ML Ops); Tom Becker (Rivermark, CTO); Marisol Vega (Rivermark, Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in to confirm uplift and geo expansion. Discussed dedicated vs hosted, VPC/on-prem options for EU, benchmarks, and procurement timeline.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time on Valentine's — appreciate it. Quick roll call? I see Aisha, Tom, Marisol — can you hear us okay?
[00:12] Aisha: Yeah good loud and clear. Sorry timezone juggling today, thanks Liam.
[00:20] Priya: Hey all, Priya from Redwood SE, I'll be the deep dive person for the benchmarks and infra questions.
[00:30] Tom: Tom here. We wanted to focus this call on two things: renewal timing and adding EU and APAC regions with predictable latency. Also want to confirm data residency constraints in EU.
[00:45] Liam: Perfect. Our notes show current renewal window in late March; you were looking at bumping capacity by ~2.5x and adding EU/ASIA. Aisha, is that still accurate?
[00:58] Aisha: Yep roughly. We saw token volumes climb after the holiday release — burst patterns are heavier. We're hitting token throttles on hosted and some tail p95 latency concerns during peak merchandising requests.
[01:18] Priya: When you say p95 are we talking end-to-end application p95 or model generation? Also what's typical seq length and batch sizes?
[01:30] Aisha: Model generation p95, around 400–600ms now on hosted for our primary LLM, seq lens average 512 tokens, sometimes 1k for long form. Batch sizes small — many customer-facing single-turn calls.
[01:50] Liam: Ok that explains the desire for dedicated — predictable GPU pooling helps with tail. Quick qual: are you leaning dedicated reserved capacity or private VPC/onprem?
[02:05] Tom: Ideally dedicated first for throughput and then private VPC for EU compliance. For APAC we just need region presence; private isn't required there yet.
[02:20] Marisol: From procurement, we prefer a single contract amendment if possible — fewer SOWs. Also need vendor attestation docs (SOC2, ISO) and sample amendment text early.
[02:35] Liam: We'll send SOC2/ISO and a draft amendment. Priya, can you confirm what perf delta we'd expect moving to dedicated with our seq lens?
[02:50] Priya: Short answer — p95 should drop to ~220–320ms depending on model and KV cache heat. With continuous batching and prefix cache we see 20–40% cost reduction per token in similar workloads. But note warm-up on new region can add some cold start noise.
[03:12] Aisha: 20–40% cost reduction sounds promising. Can you do a benchmark using our prompt set? We want end-to-end numbers that include our pre/post-processing.
[03:25] Priya: Absolutely — if you share the prompt set and a small sample traffic replay we can run a reproducible bench on dedicated infra and a private VPC variant.
[03:40] Aisha: I'll drop a sanitized sample to the repo link we shared earlier. Also need to surface our SAML SSO requirements and audit log retention for the EU region.
[03:55] Liam: On SSO we support SAML and OIDC, RBAC via console, and audit logs exportable to your SIEM. We'll include retention options; longer retention is an add-on.
[04:10] Tom: For EU data residency we need the control plane metadata to be within EU — is that possible for a private control plane deploy?
[04:22] Priya: Yes private control plane places metadata within customer VPC/region; for hosted we can commit region pinning but audit trails still transit our control plane. We'll share the private deployment checklist.
[04:40] Marisol: Timeline question: procurement needs 30 days lead for contracts. If we sign an amendment mid‑March, can you guarantee region activation by end of Q2?
[04:55] Liam: End of Q2 for EU + APAC depends on capacity pool availability — typical lead 4–8 weeks after contract, APAC sometimes slightly longer. We'll aim for Q2 end but will make it contractual on the amendment with milestone dates.
[05:15] Aisha: For sizing, we are projecting steady state 1.2k qps with peaks to 3k qps. That's across three primary endpoints. We can narrow down if needed.
[05:30] Priya: Good — that's actionable. For the bench we'll provision a dedicated pool approximating 30–40% headroom over steady state to mimic peaks.
[05:45] Liam: Marisol, can you confirm billing preference? Net30? PO reference? Anything special?
[05:55] Marisol: Net30 preferred. We'll include a PO and supplier forms after we see the amendment. Also we'd like a clause for early termination if regulatory requires onprem move.
[06:10] Tom: One more technical — do you offer per-route model pinning and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants if capacity constrained?
[06:25] Priya: Yes per-route pinning and automated fallbacks are supported; we can configure A/B rollouts so you can test fallbacks. Quantized variants give lower latency but can change output quality; we'll include QoE evals in the bench.
[06:45] Aisha: QoE evals are critical. We have a set of golden prompts and expected outputs — we'll share that.

-- mid-call check --
[07:05] Liam: High level next steps: SE runs benchmark on dedicated and private VPC, AE drafts amendment and pricing workbook, procurement shares PO template. Any blockers?
[07:18] Marisol: Need SOC2 doc and customer references for private deploys — if you have any fintech customers in EU who did private control plane, that helps.
[07:30] Liam: We'll redact references and share as case studies. Also we'll include the KMS/ HSM integration notes.
[07:42] Priya: For the bench, it would help to get a traffic replay and a short runbook of any pre/post processing steps so our numbers are E2E.
[07:55] Aisha: You'll get that tonight. Expect a sanitized subset.

[20:10] Priya: (after running some remote checks) Quick note — GPU type matters for your seq len. For 1k sequence workloads we recommend A100 or equivalent; for 512 avg lens a mix of 80GB and 40GB works well. We'll put hardware mapping in the bench report.
[20:30] Tom: Cost sensitivity: we need to keep unit cost per 1k tokens below our current blended cost or provide offset by latency improvements.
[20:45] Liam: Understood. The pricing workbook will show preferred configs and tiered discounts for reserved capacity; we'll simulate cost per token with and without quantization.

[31:00] Marisol: Legal question — can you accept data processing addendum with specific EU-centric clauses, and any standard indemnities for PII exposures?
[31:14] Liam: We have a standard DPA and can add EU-specific clauses; indemnity language is negotiable, but severe liability clauses are typically capped. We'll circulate suggested wording.

[36:05] Aisha: Regarding monitoring — do you expose token-level cost and latency by API token and route? We want per-team chargeback.
[36:20] Priya: Yes Console has token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can provide an ingestion hook to your chargeback system.
[36:35] Tom: Any limits on audit log retention sizes or search exports?
[36:45] Liam: Retention windows are flexible; export via S3 or SIEM connector. Longer retention has an extra fee; we'll note that in the amendment.

[41:00] Priya: To summarize technical deliverables — we will run bench on dedicated pool and private VPC, include QoE evals, hardware mapping, and region warm-up guidance.
[41:15] Liam: Commercially we'll draft a 9‑month amendment with EU/APAC addendum and proposed capacity uplift. We'll include milestone dates and activation SLAs.
[41:30] Marisol: Sounds good. Let's aim to close the amendment two weeks before your current renewal window to avoid service interruption.
[41:42] Liam: Agreed. We'll target sharing docs by 2025-02-20 and reconvene on 2025-02-24 to review bench and contract.

[47:10] Aisha: One last bit — we'd like an optional add-on for third-party penetration testing coordination. Is that supported?
[47:22] Priya: Yes we can coordinate and provide a scoped test plan and host contact. There may be blackout windows for heavy benching.
[47:35] Tom: Ok thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[47:40] Liam: Thanks all. We'll follow up with SOC2 links, pricing workbook, bench invite, and draft amendment. Bye for now.
[47:50] Marisol: Bye

References/Links shared in call:
- Pricing workbook (draft): https://redwood.example/pricing/rivermark-workbook
- SOC2 & ISO attestations: https://redwood.example/compliance/soc2.pdf
- Private deployment checklist: https://redwood.example/docs/private-checklist

End of transcript
